**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](/wiki/Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](/wiki/Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](/wiki/Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

Stadium
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Stadium")]

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

The club was founded in 1923 but ceased to exist in 2020 after going bankrupt.[[2]](#cite_note-hln-2) A few days after the bankruptcy, the club announced that rather than dissolving entirely, it would merge with KSV Temse to form [Lokeren-Temse](/wiki/K.S.C._Lokeren-Temse \"K.S.C. Lokeren-Temse\"), starting in the [Belgian Second Amateur Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Amateur_Division \"Belgian Second Amateur Division\") (fourth level).[[3]](#cite_note-sporza-3)\\n\\nLokeren first reached the first division in [1974–75](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_1974-75 \"Belgian First Division 1974-75\"). Since then, it had a short spell in the [Second Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Division \"Belgian Second Division\") between [1993–94](/w/index.php?title=1993%E2%80%9394_in_Belgian_football&action=edit&redlink=1 \"1993–94 in Belgian football (page does not exist)\") and [1995–96](/w/index.php?title=1995%E2%80%9396_in_Belgian_football&action=edit&redlink=1 \"1995–96 in Belgian football (page does not exist)\"). Lokeren had its most successful period in the 1980s, achieving second place in the league in [1980–81](/wiki/1980%E2%80%9381_Belgian_First_Division \"1980–81 Belgian First Division\") as well as a [Belgian Cup](/wiki/Belgian_Cup \"Belgian Cup\") final the same year. Its best European result was reaching the quarter-final of the [1980–81 UEFA Cup](/wiki/1980%E2%80%9381_UEFA_Cup \"1980–81 UEFA Cup\"). In the year 2000, the club merged with [K Sint-Niklase SKE](/wiki/K._Sint-Niklase_S.K.E. \"K. Sint-Niklase S.K.E.\"). They were registered to the [Royal Belgian Football Association](/wiki/Royal_Belgian_Football_Association \"Royal Belgian Football Association\") with the [matricule number](/wiki/Matricule \"Matricule\") 282. Lokeren\\'s colours were white, black and yellow. They played their home games at the [Daknamstadion](/wiki/Daknamstadion \"Daknamstadion\").\\n\\nIn 2012, Sporting Lokeren won the Belgian Cup, the club\\'s first-ever honours, after beating [KV Kortrijk](/wiki/KV_Kortrijk \"KV Kortrijk\") in the Cup Final. They won their second Cup just two years later, after beating [Zulte Waregem](/wiki/S.V._Zulte_Waregem \"S.V. Zulte Waregem\") 1–0.\\n\\nHistory\\n-------\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=K.S.C._Lokeren_Oost-Vlaanderen&action=edit&section=1 \"Edit section: History\")]\\n\\nThe matricule No. 282 was given in [1920](/wiki/1920_in_association_football \"1920 in association football\") to a club named Football Club Racing Club Lokeren (nicknamed Racing FC), but the team stopped its activity the next year. On [22 January 1923](/wiki/1923_in_association_football \"1923 in association football\") Racing Club Lokeren was founded. Between [1945](/wiki/1945_in_association_football \"1945 in association football\") and [1951](/wiki/1951_in_association_football \"1951 in association football\"), it had a slight name change (to Racing Athletiek- en Football Club Lokeren) and the new name since 1951 was Koninklijke Racing Club Lokeren. Due to financial problems, the fusion with the other team from the town (Koninklijke Standaard FC Lokeren) became necessary in [1970](/wiki/1970_in_association_football \"1970 in association football\"). The new club was then named Koninklijke Sporting Club Lokeren.\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png/250px-KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png)](/wiki/File:KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png)\\n\\nHistorical chart of KSC\\xa0Lokeren league performance\\n\\nIn 2000, the club merged with Koninklijke Sint-Niklaas SKE to form Sporting Lokeren Sint-Niklaas Waasland. The latest name change occurred in [2003](/wiki/2003_in_association_football \"2003 in association football\"), with the province name added to the club name.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*]\\n\\nIn 2018, Sporting Lokeren were relegated to the [First Division B](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_B \"Belgian First Division B\"), the second tier of Belgian football.[[4]](#cite_note-4) In 2019, the club was taken over by a group led by Louis de Vries and Alexander Janssen, taking the positions of president and CEO respectively.\\n\\nOn 20 April 2020, the club was declared bankrupt during the 2019–20 season.[[2]](#cite_note-hln-2) Lokeren had outstanding debts of €5 million and was not able to pay its staff and players anymore.\\n\\nOn 22 April 2020, Lokeren agreed to merge with KSV Temse to form a new club in [K.S.C. Lokeren-Temse](/wiki/K.S.C._Lokeren-Temse \"K.S.C. Westerlo season\")* | |\\n\\n**[Koninklijke](/wiki/Koninklijk \"Koninklijk\") Voetbal Club Westerlo** (Dutch pronunciation: [[ˈkoːnɪŋkləkə ˈvudbɑl ˌklʏp ˈʋɛstərloː]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Dutch \"Help:IPA/Dutch\"); often simply called **Westerlo**) is a [Belgian](/wiki/Belgium \"Belgium\") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football \"Association football\") club located in the municipality of [Westerlo](/wiki/Westerlo \"Westerlo\") in the province of [Antwerp](/wiki/Antwerp_(province) \"Antwerp (province)\"). Since [1997–98](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_1997-98 \"Belgian First Division 1997-98\"), Westerlo has been mostly playing in the [Belgian Pro League](/wiki/Belgian_Pro_League \"Belgian Pro League\"), save for a short stint in the [Belgian Second Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Division \"Belgian Second Division\") between 2012 and 2014. Their highest finish is a 6th place in [1999–00](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_1999-2000 \"Belgian First Division 1999-2000\"), [2003–04](/wiki/2003%E2%80%9304_Belgian_First_Division \"2003–04 Belgian First Division\") and [2008–09](/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_Belgian_First_Division \"2008–09 Belgian First Division\"). They have won one [Belgian Cup](/wiki/Belgian_Cup \"Belgian Cup\"). The only player who has ever been called up for the [Belgium national football team](/wiki/Belgium_national_football_team \"Belgium national football team\") while at Westerlo is [Toni Brogno](/wiki/Toni_Brogno \"Toni Brogno\") (7 caps, all of them while at Westerlo).\\n\\nThe club was founded in 1933, receiving the [matricule number](/wiki/Football_in_Belgium#Matricule_numbers \"Football in Belgium\") 2024. Their colours are yellow and blue. They play their home matches at the [Het Kuipje](/wiki/Het_Kuipje \"Het Kuipje\").\\n\\nHistory\\n-------\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=K.V.C._Westerlo&action=edit&section=1 \"Edit section: History\")]\\n\\n**K.V.C. Westerlo** was founded in the city of Westerlo by students in 1917, and it was named Sportkring De Bist Westerlo. After five years of existence, the club retired. The club **Bist Sport** was created in 1931 and it changed its name to Sportkring Westerlo two years later. At that time. some players left the club to found **Westerlo Sport**, the ancestor of **K.V.C. Westerlo**. In 1939, the club won its [league](/wiki/Belgian_Provincial_leagues \"Belgian Provincial leagues\") for the first time. Five years later, Sportkring Westerlo and dissident Westerlo Sport decided to merge in spite of the rivalry between the teams, and the new club was called **V.C. Westerlo**.\\n\\nIt became champion of the [Antwerp second division](/wiki/Belgian_Provincial_leagues \"Belgian Provincial leagues\") in 1960. Eight years later it played its first season at the national level in [Promotion](/wiki/Belgian_Promotion \"Belgian Promotion\") and it won its league to play the [third division](/wiki/Belgian_Third_Division \"Belgian Third Division\") in 1969. At the end of the season, Westerlo missed a third title in a row, finishing second behind [Eupen](/wiki/K.A.S._Eupen \"K.A.S. Eupen\"). The next year, the club was relegated after the playoff and it stayed in the Promotion for ten seasons. The club then underwent two relegations in a row and thus played in the Antwerp second division in 1982–83. Westerlo was then promoted for three consecutive years to qualify for the third division once again. In 1993, the club promoted to the [second division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Division \"Belgian Second Division\") and then to the first division in 1997. In 1996, the club added the prefix *[Koninklijke](/wiki/Koninklijk \"Koninklijk\")* (meaning \"Royal\" in [Dutch](/wiki/Dutch_language \"Dutch language\")) to its name.\\n\\nOn 18 June 2019 it was officially announced that the club was taken over by Turkish businessman Oktay Ercan. He immediately made it clear that KVC Westerlo will remain a regional family club, and that more attention will be paid to the social dimension and sporting ambitions. \"Serbian Cyrillic alphabet\"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian \"Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian\")) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegro \"Montenegro\") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football \"Association football\") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](/wiki/Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor \"Radanovići, Kotor\"), municipality of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor \"Kotor\"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League \"Montenegrin Second League\").\\n\\nHistory\\n-------\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=1 \"Edit section: History\")]\\n\\nThe first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League \"Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)\") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia \"FR Yugoslavia\") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia \"1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia\"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  \\nAfter [Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 \"Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006\"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League \"Montenegrin First League\"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta \"FK Zeta\") and [Budućnost Podgorica](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica \"FK Budućnost Podgorica\"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn\\'t achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  \\nOFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom \"FK Kom\") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar \"FK Mornar\") in [Bar](/wiki/Bar,_Montenegro \"Bar, Montenegro\") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  \\nIn the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Montenegrin_Cup \"2016–17 Montenegrin Cup\"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 \"FK Sutjeska Nikšić\") 1–0.  \\nAfter 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League \"2019-20 Montenegrin First League\"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League \"Montenegrin Second League\").\\n\\n### First League Record\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=2 \"Edit section: First League Record\")]\\n\\nSee also: [Participants of Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League#All_time_tables \"Montenegrin First League\")\\n\\nFor the first time, OFK Grbalj played in Montenegrin First League on season [2006–07](/wiki/2006%E2%80%9307_Montenegrin_First_League \"2006–07 Montenegrin First League\"). **[Koninklijke](/wiki/Koninklijke "Koninklijke") Sporting Club Lokeren Oost-Vlaanderen** (Dutch pronunciation: [[ˈkoːnɪŋkləkə ˈspɔrtɪŋ ˌklʏp ˈloːkərən oːstˈflaːndərə(n), -rə ʔoː-]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Dutch "Help:IPA/Dutch")), often simply called **Sporting Lokeren** or **Lokeren**, was a [Belgian](/wiki/Football_in_Belgium "Football in Belgium") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in the city of [Lokeren](/wiki/Lokeren "Lokeren"), in the province of [East Flanders](/wiki/East_Flanders "East Flanders"). The club was founded in 1923 but ceased to exist in 2020 after going bankrupt.[[2]](#cite_note-hln-2) A few days after the bankruptcy, the club announced that rather than dissolving entirely, it would merge with KSV Temse to form [Lokeren-Temse](/wiki/K.S.C._Lokeren-Temse "K.S.C. Lokeren-Temse"), starting in the [Belgian Second Amateur Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Amateur_Division "Belgian Second Amateur Division") (fourth level).[[3]](#cite_note-sporza-3)

Lokeren first reached the first division in [1974–75](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_1974-75 "Belgian First Division 1974-75"). Since then, it had a short spell in the [Second Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Division "Belgian Second Division") between [1993–94](/w/index.php?title=1993%E2%80%9394_in_Belgian_football&action=edit&redlink=1 "1993–94 in Belgian football (page does not exist)") and [1995–96](/w/index.php?title=1995%E2%80%9396_in_Belgian_football&action=edit&redlink=1 "1995–96 in Belgian football (page does not exist)"). Lokeren had its most successful period in the 1980s, achieving second place in the league in [1980–81](/wiki/1980%E2%80%9381_Belgian_First_Division "1980–81 Belgian First Division") as well as a [Belgian Cup](/wiki/Belgian_Cup "Belgian Cup") final the same year. Its best European result was reaching the quarter-final of the [1980–81 UEFA Cup](/wiki/1980%E2%80%9381_UEFA_Cup "1980–81 UEFA Cup"). In the year 2000, the club merged with [K Sint-Niklase SKE](/wiki/K._Sint-Niklase_S.K.E. "K. Sint-Niklase S.K.E."). They were registered to the [Royal Belgian Football Association](/wiki/Royal_Belgian_Football_Association "Royal Belgian Football Association") with the [matricule number](/wiki/Matricule "Matricule") 282. Lokeren's colours were white, black and yellow. They played their home games at the [Daknamstadion](/wiki/Daknamstadion "Daknamstadion").

In 2012, Sporting Lokeren won the Belgian Cup, the club's first-ever honours, after beating [KV Kortrijk](/wiki/KV_Kortrijk "KV Kortrijk") in the Cup Final. They won their second Cup just two years later, after beating [Zulte Waregem](/wiki/S.V._Zulte_Waregem "S.V. Zulte Waregem") 1–0.

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=K.S.C._Lokeren_Oost-Vlaanderen&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The matricule No. 282 was given in [1920](/wiki/1920_in_association_football "1920 in association football") to a club named Football Club Racing Club Lokeren (nicknamed Racing FC), but the team stopped its activity the next year. On [22 January 1923](/wiki/1923_in_association_football "1923 in association football") Racing Club Lokeren was founded. Between [1945](/wiki/1945_in_association_football "1945 in association football") and [1951](/wiki/1951_in_association_football "1951 in association football"), it had a slight name change (to Racing Athletiek- en Football Club Lokeren) and the new name since 1951 was Koninklijke Racing Club Lokeren. Due to financial problems, the fusion with the other team from the town (Koninklijke Standaard FC Lokeren) became necessary in [1970](/wiki/1970_in_association_football "1970 in association football"). The new club was then named Koninklijke Sporting Club Lokeren.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png/250px-KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png)](/wiki/File:KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png)

Historical chart of KSC Lokeren league performance

In 2000, the club merged with Koninklijke Sint-Niklaas SKE to form Sporting Lokeren Sint-Niklaas Waasland. The latest name change occurred in [2003](/wiki/2003_in_association_football "2003 in association football"), with the province name added to the club name.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

In 2018, Sporting Lokeren were relegated to the [First Division B](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_B "Belgian First Division B"), the second tier of Belgian football.[[4]](#cite_note-4) In 2019, the club was taken over by a group led by Louis de Vries and Alexander Janssen, taking the positions of president and CEO respectively.

On 20 April 2020, the club was declared bankrupt during the 2019–20 season.[[2]](#cite_note-hln-2) Lokeren had outstanding debts of €5 million and was not able to pay its staff and players anymore.

On 22 April 2020, Lokeren agreed to merge with KSV Temse to form a new club in [K.S.C. Lokeren-Temse](/wiki/K.S.C._Lokeren-Temse "K.S.C. Lokeren-Temse") and to start in the [Second Amateur Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Amateur_Division "Belgian Second Amateur Division"), the national fourth level.[[5]](#cite_note-5)

**[Koninklijke](/wiki/Koninklijke "Koninklijke") Sporting Club Lokeren Oost-Vlaanderen** (Dutch pronunciation: [[ˈkoːnɪŋkləkə ˈspɔrtɪŋ ˌklʏp ˈloːkərən oːstˈflaːndərə(n), -rə ʔoː-]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Dutch "Help:IPA/Dutch")), often simply called **Sporting Lokeren** or **Lokeren**, was a [Belgian](/wiki/Football_in_Belgium "Football in Belgium") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in the city of [Lokeren](/wiki/Lokeren "Lokeren"), in the province of [East Flanders](/wiki/East_Flanders "East Flanders"). The club was founded in 1923 but ceased to exist in 2020 after going bankrupt.[[2]](#cite_note-hln-2) A few days after the bankruptcy, the club announced that rather than dissolving entirely, it would merge with KSV Temse to form [Lokeren-Temse](/wiki/K.S.C._Lokeren-Temse "K.S.C. Lokeren-Temse"), starting in the [Belgian Second Amateur Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Amateur_Division "Belgian Second Amateur Division") (fourth level).[[3]](#cite_note-sporza-3)

Lokeren first reached the first division in [1974–75](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_1974-75 "Belgian First Division 1974-75"). Since then, it had a short spell in the [Second Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Division "Belgian Second Division") between [1993–94](/w/index.php?title=1993%E2%80%9394_in_Belgian_football&action=edit&redlink=1 "1993–94 in Belgian football (page does not exist)") and [1995–96](/w/index.php?title=1995%E2%80%9396_in_Belgian_football&action=edit&redlink=1 "1995–96 in Belgian football (page does not exist)"). Lokeren had its most successful period in the 1980s, achieving second place in the league in [1980–81](/wiki/1980%E2%80%9381_Belgian_First_Division "1980–81 Belgian First Division") as well as a [Belgian Cup](/wiki/Belgian_Cup "Belgian Cup") final the same year. Its best European result was reaching the quarter-final of the [1980–81 UEFA Cup](/wiki/1980%E2%80%9381_UEFA_Cup "1980–81 UEFA Cup"). In the year 2000, the club merged with [K Sint-Niklase SKE](/wiki/K._Sint-Niklase_S.K.E. "K. Sint-Niklase S.K.E."). They were registered to the [Royal Belgian Football Association](/wiki/Royal_Belgian_Football_Association "Royal Belgian Football Association") with the [matricule number](/wiki/Matricule "Matricule") 282. Lokeren's colours were white, black and yellow. They played their home games at the [Daknamstadion](/wiki/Daknamstadion "Daknamstadion").

In 2012, Sporting Lokeren won the Belgian Cup, the club's first-ever honours, after beating [KV Kortrijk](/wiki/KV_Kortrijk "KV Kortrijk") in the Cup Final. They won their second Cup just two years later, after beating [Zulte Waregem](/wiki/S.V._Zulte_Waregem "S.V. Zulte Waregem") 1–0.

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=K.S.C._Lokeren_Oost-Vlaanderen&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The matricule No. 282 was given in [1920](/wiki/1920_in_association_football "1920 in association football") to a club named Football Club Racing Club Lokeren (nicknamed Racing FC), but the team stopped its activity the next year. On [22 January 1923](/wiki/1923_in_association_football "1923 in association football") Racing Club Lokeren was founded. Between [1945](/wiki/1945_in_association_football "1945 in association football") and [1951](/wiki/1951_in_association_football "1951 in association football"), it had a slight name change (to Racing Athletiek- en Football Club Lokeren) and the new name since 1951 was Koninklijke Racing Club Lokeren. Due to financial problems, the fusion with the other team from the town (Koninklijke Standaard FC Lokeren) became necessary in [1970](/wiki/1970_in_association_football "1970 in association football"). The new club was then named Koninklijke Sporting Club Lokeren.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png/250px-KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png)](/wiki/File:KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png)

Historical chart of KSC Lokeren league performance

In 2000, the club merged with Koninklijke Sint-Niklaas SKE to form Sporting Lokeren Sint-Niklaas Waasland. The latest name change occurred in [2003](/wiki/2003_in_association_football "2003 in association football"), with the province name added to the club name.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

In 2018, Sporting Lokeren were relegated to the [First Division B](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_B "Belgian First Division B"), the second tier of Belgian football.[[4]](#cite_note-4) In 2019, the club was taken over by a group led by Louis de Vries and Alexander Janssen, taking the positions of president and CEO respectively.

On 20 April 2020, the club was declared bankrupt during the 2019–20 season.[[2]](#cite_note-hln-2) Lokeren had outstanding debts of €5 million and was not able to pay its staff and players anymore.

On 22 April 2020, Lokeren agreed to merge with KSV Temse to form a new club in [K.S.C. Lokeren-Temse](/wiki/K.S.C._Lokeren-Temse "K.S.C. Lokeren-Temse") and to start in the [Second Amateur Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Amateur_Division "Belgian Second Amateur Division"), the national fourth level.[[5]](#cite_note-5)

**Alexandre Boucaut** (born 10 August 1980) is a [Belgian](/wiki/Belgian_people "Belgian people") football referee. He made his debut in the [Belgian Pro League](/wiki/Belgian_Pro_League "Belgian Pro League") at 8 February 2009 in a game between [KVC Westerlo](/wiki/KVC_Westerlo "KVC Westerlo") and [KSC Lokeren](/wiki/KSC_Lokeren "KSC Lokeren"). As profession, he's head of a bank in [Ath](/wiki/Ath "Ath").[[1]](#cite_note-1)

**[Koninklijke](/wiki/Koninklijke "Koninklijke") Sporting Club Lokeren Oost-Vlaanderen** (Dutch pronunciation: [[ˈkoːnɪŋkləkə ˈspɔrtɪŋ ˌklʏp ˈloːkərən oːstˈflaːndərə(n), -rə ʔoː-]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Dutch "Help:IPA/Dutch")), often simply called **Sporting Lokeren** or **Lokeren**, was a [Belgian](/wiki/Football_in_Belgium "Football in Belgium") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in the city of [Lokeren](/wiki/Lokeren "Lokeren"), in the province of [East Flanders](/wiki/East_Flanders "East Flanders"). The club was founded in 1923 but ceased to exist in 2020 after going bankrupt.[[2]](#cite_note-hln-2) A few days after the bankruptcy, the club announced that rather than dissolving entirely, it would merge with KSV Temse to form [Lokeren-Temse](/wiki/K.S.C._Lokeren-Temse "K.S.C. Lokeren-Temse"), starting in the [Belgian Second Amateur Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Amateur_Division "Belgian Second Amateur Division") (fourth level).[[3]](#cite_note-sporza-3)

Lokeren first reached the first division in [1974–75](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_1974-75 "Belgian First Division 1974-75"). Since then, it had a short spell in the [Second Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Division "Belgian Second Division") between [1993–94](/w/index.php?title=1993%E2%80%9394_in_Belgian_football&action=edit&redlink=1 "1993–94 in Belgian football (page does not exist)") and [1995–96](/w/index.php?title=1995%E2%80%9396_in_Belgian_football&action=edit&redlink=1 "1995–96 in Belgian football (page does not exist)"). Lokeren had its most successful period in the 1980s, achieving second place in the league in [1980–81](/wiki/1980%E2%80%9381_Belgian_First_Division "1980–81 Belgian First Division") as well as a [Belgian Cup](/wiki/Belgian_Cup "Belgian Cup") final the same year. Its best European result was reaching the quarter-final of the [1980–81 UEFA Cup](/wiki/1980%E2%80%9381_UEFA_Cup "1980–81 UEFA Cup"). In the year 2000, the club merged with [K Sint-Niklase SKE](/wiki/K._Sint-Niklase_S.K.E. "K. Sint-Niklase S.K.E."). They were registered to the [Royal Belgian Football Association](/wiki/Royal_Belgian_Football_Association "Royal Belgian Football Association") with the [matricule number](/wiki/Matricule "Matricule") 282. Lokeren's colours were white, black and yellow. They played their home games at the [Daknamstadion](/wiki/Daknamstadion "Daknamstadion").

In 2012, Sporting Lokeren won the Belgian Cup, the club's first-ever honours, after beating [KV Kortrijk](/wiki/KV_Kortrijk "KV Kortrijk") in the Cup Final. They won their second Cup just two years later, after beating [Zulte Waregem](/wiki/S.V._Zulte_Waregem "S.V. Zulte Waregem") 1–0.

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=K.S.C._Lokeren_Oost-Vlaanderen&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The matricule No. 282 was given in [1920](/wiki/1920_in_association_football "1920 in association football") to a club named Football Club Racing Club Lokeren (nicknamed Racing FC), but the team stopped its activity the next year. On [22 January 1923](/wiki/1923_in_association_football "1923 in association football") Racing Club Lokeren was founded. Between [1945](/wiki/1945_in_association_football "1945 in association football") and [1951](/wiki/1951_in_association_football "1951 in association football"), it had a slight name change (to Racing Athletiek- en Football Club Lokeren) and the new name since 1951 was Koninklijke Racing Club Lokeren. Due to financial problems, the fusion with the other team from the town (Koninklijke Standaard FC Lokeren) became necessary in [1970](/wiki/1970_in_association_football "1970 in association football"). The new club was then named Koninklijke Sporting Club Lokeren.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png/250px-KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png)](/wiki/File:KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png)

Historical chart of KSC Lokeren league performance

In 2000, the club merged with Koninklijke Sint-Niklaas SKE to form Sporting Lokeren Sint-Niklaas Waasland. The latest name change occurred in [2003](/wiki/2003_in_association_football "2003 in association football"), with the province name added to the club name.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

In 2018, Sporting Lokeren were relegated to the [First Division B](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_B "Belgian First Division B"), the second tier of Belgian football.[[4]](#cite_note-4) In 2019, the club was taken over by a group led by Louis de Vries and Alexander Janssen, taking the positions of president and CEO respectively.

On 20 April 2020, the club was declared bankrupt during the 2019–20 season.[[2]](#cite_note-hln-2) Lokeren had outstanding debts of €5 million and was not able to pay its staff and players anymore.

On 22 April 2020, Lokeren agreed to merge with KSV Temse to form a new club in [K.S.C. Lokeren-Temse](/wiki/K.S.C._Lokeren-Temse "K.S.C. Lokeren-Temse") and to start in the [Second Amateur Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Amateur_Division "Belgian Second Amateur Division"), the national fourth level.[[5]](#cite_note-5)

**[Koninklijke](/wiki/Koninklijk "Koninklijk") Voetbal Club Westerlo** (Dutch pronunciation: [[ˈkoːnɪŋkləkə ˈvudbɑl ˌklʏp ˈʋɛstərloː]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Dutch "Help:IPA/Dutch"); often simply called **Westerlo**) is a [Belgian](/wiki/Belgium "Belgium") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club located in the municipality of [Westerlo](/wiki/Westerlo "Westerlo") in the province of [Antwerp](/wiki/Antwerp_(province) "Antwerp (province)"). Since [1997–98](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_1997-98 "Belgian First Division 1997-98"), Westerlo has been mostly playing in the [Belgian Pro League](/wiki/Belgian_Pro_League "Belgian Pro League"), save for a short stint in the [Belgian Second Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Division "Belgian Second Division") between 2012 and 2014. Their highest finish is a 6th place in [1999–00](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_1999-2000 "Belgian First Division 1999-2000"), [2003–04](/wiki/2003%E2%80%9304_Belgian_First_Division "2003–04 Belgian First Division") and [2008–09](/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_Belgian_First_Division "2008–09 Belgian First Division"). They have won one [Belgian Cup](/wiki/Belgian_Cup "Belgian Cup"). The only player who has ever been called up for the [Belgium national football team](/wiki/Belgium_national_football_team "Belgium national football team") while at Westerlo is [Toni Brogno](/wiki/Toni_Brogno "Toni Brogno") (7 caps, all of them while at Westerlo).

The club was founded in 1933, receiving the [matricule number](/wiki/Football_in_Belgium#Matricule_numbers "Football in Belgium") 2024. Their colours are yellow and blue. They play their home matches at the [Het Kuipje](/wiki/Het_Kuipje "Het Kuipje").

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=K.V.C._Westerlo&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

**K.V.C. Westerlo** was founded in the city of Westerlo by students in 1917, and it was named Sportkring De Bist Westerlo. After five years of existence, the club retired. The club **Bist Sport** was created in 1931 and it changed its name to Sportkring Westerlo two years later. At that time. some players left the club to found **Westerlo Sport**, the ancestor of **K.V.C. Westerlo**. In 1939, the club won its [league](/wiki/Belgian_Provincial_leagues "Belgian Provincial leagues") for the first time. Five years later, Sportkring Westerlo and dissident Westerlo Sport decided to merge in spite of the rivalry between the teams, and the new club was called **V.C. Westerlo**.

It became champion of the [Antwerp second division](/wiki/Belgian_Provincial_leagues "Belgian Provincial leagues") in 1960. Eight years later it played its first season at the national level in [Promotion](/wiki/Belgian_Promotion "Belgian Promotion") and it won its league to play the [third division](/wiki/Belgian_Third_Division "Belgian Third Division") in 1969. At the end of the season, Westerlo missed a third title in a row, finishing second behind [Eupen](/wiki/K.A.S._Eupen "K.A.S. Eupen"). The next year, the club was relegated after the playoff and it stayed in the Promotion for ten seasons. The club then underwent two relegations in a row and thus played in the Antwerp second division in 1982–83. Westerlo was then promoted for three consecutive years to qualify for the third division once again. In 1993, the club promoted to the [second division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Division "Belgian Second Division") and then to the first division in 1997. In 1996, the club added the prefix *[Koninklijke](/wiki/Koninklijk "Koninklijk")* (meaning "Royal" in [Dutch](/wiki/Dutch_language "Dutch language")) to its name.

On 18 June 2019 it was officially announced that the club was taken over by Turkish businessman Oktay Ercan. He immediately made it clear that KVC Westerlo will remain a regional family club, and that more attention will be paid to the social dimension and sporting ambitions. Ercan expressed his commitment in 2019 to a year-long plan called 'KVC Westerlo 2024'.[[2]](#cite_note-2)

Stadium
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=K.V.C._Westerlo&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Stadium")]

Westerlo plays its home matches at [Het Kuipje](/wiki/Het_Kuipje "Het Kuipje"), which is Dutch for "The Cockpit". Its capacity is 8,035.[[1]](#cite_note-auto-1)

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](/wiki/Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](/wiki/Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](/wiki/Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

### OFK Grbalj in European competitions

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: OFK Grbalj in European competitions")]

For the first time, OFK Grbalj played in European competitions on season [2007-08](/wiki/2007_UEFA_Intertoto_Cup "2007 UEFA Intertoto Cup").  
They were first team from Montenegrin coastal region which played in [UEFA](/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") competitions. Until now, OFK Grbalj played two seasons in European cups.

Stadium
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Stadium")]

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**[Koninklijke](/wiki/Koninklijke "Koninklijke") Sporting Club Lokeren Oost-Vlaanderen** (Dutch pronunciation: [[ˈkoːnɪŋkləkə ˈspɔrtɪŋ ˌklʏp ˈloːkərən oːstˈflaːndərə(n), -rə ʔoː-]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Dutch "Help:IPA/Dutch")), often simply called **Sporting Lokeren** or **Lokeren**, was a [Belgian](/wiki/Football_in_Belgium "Football in Belgium") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in the city of [Lokeren](/wiki/Lokeren "Lokeren"), in the province of [East Flanders](/wiki/East_Flanders "East Flanders"). The club was founded in 1923 but ceased to exist in 2020 after going bankrupt.[[2]](#cite_note-hln-2) A few days after the bankruptcy, the club announced that rather than dissolving entirely, it would merge with KSV Temse to form [Lokeren-Temse](/wiki/K.S.C._Lokeren-Temse "K.S.C. Lokeren-Temse"), starting in the [Belgian Second Amateur Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Amateur_Division "Belgian Second Amateur Division") (fourth level).[[3]](#cite_note-sporza-3)

Lokeren first reached the first division in [1974–75](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_1974-75 "Belgian First Division 1974-75"). Since then, it had a short spell in the [Second Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Division "Belgian Second Division") between [1993–94](/w/index.php?title=1993%E2%80%9394_in_Belgian_football&action=edit&redlink=1 "1993–94 in Belgian football (page does not exist)") and [1995–96](/w/index.php?title=1995%E2%80%9396_in_Belgian_football&action=edit&redlink=1 "1995–96 in Belgian football (page does not exist)"). Lokeren had its most successful period in the 1980s, achieving second place in the league in [1980–81](/wiki/1980%E2%80%9381_Belgian_First_Division "1980–81 Belgian First Division") as well as a [Belgian Cup](/wiki/Belgian_Cup "Belgian Cup") final the same year. Its best European result was reaching the quarter-final of the [1980–81 UEFA Cup](/wiki/1980%E2%80%9381_UEFA_Cup "1980–81 UEFA Cup"). In the year 2000, the club merged with [K Sint-Niklase SKE](/wiki/K._Sint-Niklase_S.K.E. "K. Sint-Niklase S.K.E."). They were registered to the [Royal Belgian Football Association](/wiki/Royal_Belgian_Football_Association "Royal Belgian Football Association") with the [matricule number](/wiki/Matricule "Matricule") 282. Lokeren's colours were white, black and yellow. They played their home games at the [Daknamstadion](/wiki/Daknamstadion "Daknamstadion").

In 2012, Sporting Lokeren won the Belgian Cup, the club's first-ever honours, after beating [KV Kortrijk](/wiki/KV_Kortrijk "KV Kortrijk") in the Cup Final. They won their second Cup just two years later, after beating [Zulte Waregem](/wiki/S.V._Zulte_Waregem "S.V. Zulte Waregem") 1–0.

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=K.S.C._Lokeren_Oost-Vlaanderen&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The matricule No. 282 was given in [1920](/wiki/1920_in_association_football "1920 in association football") to a club named Football Club Racing Club Lokeren (nicknamed Racing FC), but the team stopped its activity the next year. On [22 January 1923](/wiki/1923_in_association_football "1923 in association football") Racing Club Lokeren was founded. Between [1945](/wiki/1945_in_association_football "1945 in association football") and [1951](/wiki/1951_in_association_football "1951 in association football"), it had a slight name change (to Racing Athletiek- en Football Club Lokeren) and the new name since 1951 was Koninklijke Racing Club Lokeren. Due to financial problems, the fusion with the other team from the town (Koninklijke Standaard FC Lokeren) became necessary in [1970](/wiki/1970_in_association_football "1970 in association football"). The new club was then named Koninklijke Sporting Club Lokeren.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png/250px-KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png)](/wiki/File:KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png)

Historical chart of KSC Lokeren league performance

In 2000, the club merged with Koninklijke Sint-Niklaas SKE to form Sporting Lokeren Sint-Niklaas Waasland. The latest name change occurred in [2003](/wiki/2003_in_association_football "2003 in association football"), with the province name added to the club name.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

In 2018, Sporting Lokeren were relegated to the [First Division B](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_B "Belgian First Division B"), the second tier of Belgian football.[[4]](#cite_note-4) In 2019, the club was taken over by a group led by Louis de Vries and Alexander Janssen, taking the positions of president and CEO respectively.

On 20 April 2020, the club was declared bankrupt during the 2019–20 season.[[2]](#cite_note-hln-2) Lokeren had outstanding debts of €5 million and was not able to pay its staff and players anymore.

On 22 April 2020, Lokeren agreed to merge with KSV Temse to form a new club in [K.S.C. Lokeren-Temse](/wiki/K.S.C._Lokeren-Temse "K.S.C. Lokeren-Temse") and to start in the [Second Amateur Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Amateur_Division "Belgian Second Amateur Division"), the national fourth level.[[5]](#cite_note-5)

**Alexandre Boucaut** (born 10 August 1980) is a [Belgian](/wiki/Belgian_people "Belgian people") football referee. He made his debut in the [Belgian Pro League](/wiki/Belgian_Pro_League "Belgian Pro League") at 8 February 2009 in a game between [KVC Westerlo](/wiki/KVC_Westerlo "KVC Westerlo") and [KSC Lokeren](/wiki/KSC_Lokeren "KSC Lokeren"). As profession, he's head of a bank in [Ath](/wiki/Ath "Ath").[[1]](#cite_note-1)

**[Koninklijke](/wiki/Koninklijke "Koninklijke") Sporting Club Lokeren Oost-Vlaanderen** (Dutch pronunciation: [[ˈkoːnɪŋkləkə ˈspɔrtɪŋ ˌklʏp ˈloːkərən oːstˈflaːndərə(n), -rə ʔoː-]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Dutch "Help:IPA/Dutch")), often simply called **Sporting Lokeren** or **Lokeren**, was a [Belgian](/wiki/Football_in_Belgium "Football in Belgium") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in the city of [Lokeren](/wiki/Lokeren "Lokeren"), in the province of [East Flanders](/wiki/East_Flanders "East Flanders"). The club was founded in 1923 but ceased to exist in 2020 after going bankrupt.[[2]](#cite_note-hln-2) A few days after the bankruptcy, the club announced that rather than dissolving entirely, it would merge with KSV Temse to form [Lokeren-Temse](/wiki/K.S.C._Lokeren-Temse "K.S.C. Lokeren-Temse"), starting in the [Belgian Second Amateur Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Amateur_Division "Belgian Second Amateur Division") (fourth level).[[3]](#cite_note-sporza-3)

Lokeren first reached the first division in [1974–75](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_1974-75 "Belgian First Division 1974-75"). Since then, it had a short spell in the [Second Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Division "Belgian Second Division") between [1993–94](/w/index.php?title=1993%E2%80%9394_in_Belgian_football&action=edit&redlink=1 "1993–94 in Belgian football (page does not exist)") and [1995–96](/w/index.php?title=1995%E2%80%9396_in_Belgian_football&action=edit&redlink=1 "1995–96 in Belgian football (page does not exist)"). Lokeren had its most successful period in the 1980s, achieving second place in the league in [1980–81](/wiki/1980%E2%80%9381_Belgian_First_Division "1980–81 Belgian First Division") as well as a [Belgian Cup](/wiki/Belgian_Cup "Belgian Cup") final the same year. Its best European result was reaching the quarter-final of the [1980–81 UEFA Cup](/wiki/1980%E2%80%9381_UEFA_Cup "1980–81 UEFA Cup"). In the year 2000, the club merged with [K Sint-Niklase SKE](/wiki/K._Sint-Niklase_S.K.E. "K. Sint-Niklase S.K.E."). They were registered to the [Royal Belgian Football Association](/wiki/Royal_Belgian_Football_Association "Royal Belgian Football Association") with the [matricule number](/wiki/Matricule "Matricule") 282. Lokeren's colours were white, black and yellow. They played their home games at the [Daknamstadion](/wiki/Daknamstadion "Daknamstadion").

In 2012, Sporting Lokeren won the Belgian Cup, the club's first-ever honours, after beating [KV Kortrijk](/wiki/KV_Kortrijk "KV Kortrijk") in the Cup Final. They won their second Cup just two years later, after beating [Zulte Waregem](/wiki/S.V._Zulte_Waregem "S.V. Zulte Waregem") 1–0.

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=K.S.C._Lokeren_Oost-Vlaanderen&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The matricule No. 282 was given in [1920](/wiki/1920_in_association_football "1920 in association football") to a club named Football Club Racing Club Lokeren (nicknamed Racing FC), but the team stopped its activity the next year. On [22 January 1923](/wiki/1923_in_association_football "1923 in association football") Racing Club Lokeren was founded. Between [1945](/wiki/1945_in_association_football "1945 in association football") and [1951](/wiki/1951_in_association_football "1951 in association football"), it had a slight name change (to Racing Athletiek- en Football Club Lokeren) and the new name since 1951 was Koninklijke Racing Club Lokeren. Due to financial problems, the fusion with the other team from the town (Koninklijke Standaard FC Lokeren) became necessary in [1970](/wiki/1970_in_association_football "1970 in association football"). The new club was then named Koninklijke Sporting Club Lokeren.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png/250px-KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png)](/wiki/File:KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png)

Historical chart of KSC Lokeren league performance

In 2000, the club merged with Koninklijke Sint-Niklaas SKE to form Sporting Lokeren Sint-Niklaas Waasland. The latest name change occurred in [2003](/wiki/2003_in_association_football "2003 in association football"), with the province name added to the club name.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

In 2018, Sporting Lokeren were relegated to the [First Division B](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_B "Belgian First Division B"), the second tier of Belgian football.[[4]](#cite_note-4) In 2019, the club was taken over by a group led by Louis de Vries and Alexander Janssen, taking the positions of president and CEO respectively.

On 20 April 2020, the club was declared bankrupt during the 2019–20 season.[[2]](#cite_note-hln-2) Lokeren had outstanding debts of €5 million and was not able to pay its staff and players anymore.

On 22 April 2020, Lokeren agreed to merge with KSV Temse to form a new club in [K.S.C. Lokeren-Temse](/wiki/K.S.C._Lokeren-Temse "K.S.C. Lokeren-Temse") and to start in the [Second Amateur Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Amateur_Division "Belgian Second Amateur Division"), the national fourth level.[[5]](#cite_note-5)

**[Koninklijke](/wiki/Koninklijk "Koninklijk") Voetbal Club Westerlo** (Dutch pronunciation: [[ˈkoːnɪŋkləkə ˈvudbɑl ˌklʏp ˈʋɛstərloː]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Dutch "Help:IPA/Dutch"); often simply called **Westerlo**) is a [Belgian](/wiki/Belgium "Belgium") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club located in the municipality of [Westerlo](/wiki/Westerlo "Westerlo") in the province of [Antwerp](/wiki/Antwerp_(province) "Antwerp (province)"). Since [1997–98](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_1997-98 "Belgian First Division 1997-98"), Westerlo has been mostly playing in the [Belgian Pro League](/wiki/Belgian_Pro_League "Belgian Pro League"), save for a short stint in the [Belgian Second Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Division "Belgian Second Division") between 2012 and 2014. Their highest finish is a 6th place in [1999–00](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_1999-2000 "Belgian First Division 1999-2000"), [2003–04](/wiki/2003%E2%80%9304_Belgian_First_Division "2003–04 Belgian First Division") and [2008–09](/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_Belgian_First_Division "2008–09 Belgian First Division"). They have won one [Belgian Cup](/wiki/Belgian_Cup "Belgian Cup"). The only player who has ever been called up for the [Belgium national football team](/wiki/Belgium_national_football_team "Belgium national football team") while at Westerlo is [Toni Brogno](/wiki/Toni_Brogno "Toni Brogno") (7 caps, all of them while at Westerlo).

The club was founded in 1933, receiving the [matricule number](/wiki/Football_in_Belgium#Matricule_numbers "Football in Belgium") 2024. Their colours are yellow and blue. They play their home matches at the [Het Kuipje](/wiki/Het_Kuipje "Het Kuipje").

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=K.V.C._Westerlo&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

**K.V.C. Westerlo** was founded in the city of Westerlo by students in 1917, and it was named Sportkring De Bist Westerlo. After five years of existence, the club retired. The club **Bist Sport** was created in 1931 and it changed its name to Sportkring Westerlo two years later. At that time. some players left the club to found **Westerlo Sport**, the ancestor of **K.V.C. Westerlo**. In 1939, the club won its [league](/wiki/Belgian_Provincial_leagues "Belgian Provincial leagues") for the first time. Five years later, Sportkring Westerlo and dissident Westerlo Sport decided to merge in spite of the rivalry between the teams, and the new club was called **V.C. Westerlo**.

It became champion of the [Antwerp second division](/wiki/Belgian_Provincial_leagues "Belgian Provincial leagues") in 1960. Eight years later it played its first season at the national level in [Promotion](/wiki/Belgian_Promotion "Belgian Promotion") and it won its league to play the [third division](/wiki/Belgian_Third_Division "Belgian Third Division") in 1969. At the end of the season, Westerlo missed a third title in a row, finishing second behind [Eupen](/wiki/K.A.S._Eupen "K.A.S. Eupen"). The next year, the club was relegated after the playoff and it stayed in the Promotion for ten seasons. The club then underwent two relegations in a row and thus played in the Antwerp second division in 1982–83. Westerlo was then promoted for three consecutive years to qualify for the third division once again. In 1993, the club promoted to the [second division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Division "Belgian Second Division") and then to the first division in 1997. In 1996, the club added the prefix *[Koninklijke](/wiki/Koninklijk "Koninklijk")* (meaning "Royal" in [Dutch](/wiki/Dutch_language "Dutch language")) to its name.

On 18 June 2019 it was officially announced that the club was taken over by Turkish businessman Oktay Ercan. He immediately made it clear that KVC Westerlo will remain a regional family club, and that more attention will be paid to the social dimension and sporting ambitions. Ercan expressed his commitment in 2019 to a year-long plan called 'KVC Westerlo 2024'.[[2]](#cite_note-2)

Stadium
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=K.V.C._Westerlo&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Stadium")]

Westerlo plays its home matches at [Het Kuipje](/wiki/Het_Kuipje "Het Kuipje"), which is Dutch for "The Cockpit". Its capacity is 8,035.[[1]](#cite_note-auto-1)

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](/wiki/Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](/wiki/Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](/wiki/Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

Stadium
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Stadium")]

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**[Koninklijke](/wiki/Koninklijke "Koninklijke") Sporting Club Lokeren Oost-Vlaanderen** (Dutch pronunciation: [[ˈkoːnɪŋkləkə ˈspɔrtɪŋ ˌklʏp ˈloːkərən oːstˈflaːndərə(n), -rə ʔoː-]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Dutch "Help:IPA/Dutch")), often simply called **Sporting Lokeren** or **Lokeren**, was a [Belgian](/wiki/Football_in_Belgium "Football in Belgium") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in the city of [Lokeren](/wiki/Lokeren "Lokeren"), in the province of [East Flanders](/wiki/East_Flanders "East Flanders"). The club was founded in 1923 but ceased to exist in 2020 after going bankrupt.[[2]](#cite_note-hln-2) A few days after the bankruptcy, the club announced that rather than dissolving entirely, it would merge with KSV Temse to form [Lokeren-Temse](/wiki/K.S.C._Lokeren-Temse "K.S.C. Lokeren-Temse"), starting in the [Belgian Second Amateur Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Amateur_Division "Belgian Second Amateur Division") (fourth level).[[3]](#cite_note-sporza-3)

Lokeren first reached the first division in [1974–75](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_1974-75 "Belgian First Division 1974-75"). Since then, it had a short spell in the [Second Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Division "Belgian Second Division") between [1993–94](/w/index.php?title=1993%E2%80%9394_in_Belgian_football&action=edit&redlink=1 "1993–94 in Belgian football (page does not exist)") and [1995–96](/w/index.php?title=1995%E2%80%9396_in_Belgian_football&action=edit&redlink=1 "1995–96 in Belgian football (page does not exist)"). Lokeren had its most successful period in the 1980s, achieving second place in the league in [1980–81](/wiki/1980%E2%80%9381_Belgian_First_Division "1980–81 Belgian First Division") as well as a [Belgian Cup](/wiki/Belgian_Cup "Belgian Cup") final the same year. Its best European result was reaching the quarter-final of the [1980–81 UEFA Cup](/wiki/1980%E2%80%9381_UEFA_Cup "1980–81 UEFA Cup"). In the year 2000, the club merged with [K Sint-Niklase SKE](/wiki/K._Sint-Niklase_S.K.E. "K. Sint-Niklase S.K.E."). They were registered to the [Royal Belgian Football Association](/wiki/Royal_Belgian_Football_Association "Royal Belgian Football Association") with the [matricule number](/wiki/Matricule "Matricule") 282. Lokeren's colours were white, black and yellow. They played their home games at the [Daknamstadion](/wiki/Daknamstadion "Daknamstadion").

In 2012, Sporting Lokeren won the Belgian Cup, the club's first-ever honours, after beating [KV Kortrijk](/wiki/KV_Kortrijk "KV Kortrijk") in the Cup Final. They won their second Cup just two years later, after beating [Zulte Waregem](/wiki/S.V._Zulte_Waregem "S.V. Zulte Waregem") 1–0.

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=K.S.C._Lokeren_Oost-Vlaanderen&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The matricule No. 282 was given in [1920](/wiki/1920_in_association_football "1920 in association football") to a club named Football Club Racing Club Lokeren (nicknamed Racing FC), but the team stopped its activity the next year. On [22 January 1923](/wiki/1923_in_association_football "1923 in association football") Racing Club Lokeren was founded. Between [1945](/wiki/1945_in_association_football "1945 in association football") and [1951](/wiki/1951_in_association_football "1951 in association football"), it had a slight name change (to Racing Athletiek- en Football Club Lokeren) and the new name since 1951 was Koninklijke Racing Club Lokeren. Due to financial problems, the fusion with the other team from the town (Koninklijke Standaard FC Lokeren) became necessary in [1970](/wiki/1970_in_association_football "1970 in association football"). The new club was then named Koninklijke Sporting Club Lokeren.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png/250px-KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png)](/wiki/File:KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png)

Historical chart of KSC Lokeren league performance

In 2000, the club merged with Koninklijke Sint-Niklaas SKE to form Sporting Lokeren Sint-Niklaas Waasland. The latest name change occurred in [2003](/wiki/2003_in_association_football "2003 in association football"), with the province name added to the club name.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

In 2018, Sporting Lokeren were relegated to the [First Division B](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_B "Belgian First Division B"), the second tier of Belgian football.[[4]](#cite_note-4) In 2019, the club was taken over by a group led by Louis de Vries and Alexander Janssen, taking the positions of president and CEO respectively.

On 20 April 2020, the club was declared bankrupt during the 2019–20 season.[[2]](#cite_note-hln-2) Lokeren had outstanding debts of €5 million and was not able to pay its staff and players anymore.

On 22 April 2020, Lokeren agreed to merge with KSV Temse to form a new club in [K.S.C. Lokeren-Temse](/wiki/K.S.C._Lokeren-Temse "K.S.C. Lokeren-Temse") and to start in the [Second Amateur Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Amateur_Division "Belgian Second Amateur Division"), the national fourth level.[[5]](#cite_note-5)

The club was founded in 1923 but ceased to exist in 2020 after going bankrupt.[[2]](#cite_note-hln-2) A few days after the bankruptcy, the club announced that rather than dissolving entirely, it would merge with KSV Temse to form [Lokeren-Temse](/wiki/K.S.C._Lokeren-Temse \"K.S.C. Lokeren-Temse\"), starting in the [Belgian Second Amateur Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Amateur_Division \"Belgian Second Amateur Division\") (fourth level).[[3]](#cite_note-sporza-3)\\n\\nLokeren first reached the first division in [1974–75](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_1974-75 \"Belgian First Division 1974-75\"). Since then, it had a short spell in the [Second Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Division \"Belgian Second Division\") between [1993–94](/w/index.php?title=1993%E2%80%9394_in_Belgian_football&action=edit&redlink=1 \"1993–94 in Belgian football (page does not exist)\") and [1995–96](/w/index.php?title=1995%E2%80%9396_in_Belgian_football&action=edit&redlink=1 \"1995–96 in Belgian football (page does not exist)\"). Lokeren had its most successful period in the 1980s, achieving second place in the league in [1980–81](/wiki/1980%E2%80%9381_Belgian_First_Division \"1980–81 Belgian First Division\") as well as a [Belgian Cup](/wiki/Belgian_Cup \"Belgian Cup\") final the same year. Its best European result was reaching the quarter-final of the [1980–81 UEFA Cup](/wiki/1980%E2%80%9381_UEFA_Cup \"1980–81 UEFA Cup\"). In the year 2000, the club merged with [K Sint-Niklase SKE](/wiki/K._Sint-Niklase_S.K.E. \"K. Sint-Niklase S.K.E.\"). They were registered to the [Royal Belgian Football Association](/wiki/Royal_Belgian_Football_Association \"Royal Belgian Football Association\") with the [matricule number](/wiki/Matricule \"Matricule\") 282. Lokeren\\'s colours were white, black and yellow. They played their home games at the [Daknamstadion](/wiki/Daknamstadion \"Daknamstadion\").\\n\\nIn 2012, Sporting Lokeren won the Belgian Cup, the club\\'s first-ever honours, after beating [KV Kortrijk](/wiki/KV_Kortrijk \"KV Kortrijk\") in the Cup Final. They won their second Cup just two years later, after beating [Zulte Waregem](/wiki/S.V._Zulte_Waregem \"S.V. Zulte Waregem\") 1–0.\\n\\nHistory\\n-------\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=K.S.C._Lokeren_Oost-Vlaanderen&action=edit&section=1 \"Edit section: History\")]\\n\\nThe matricule No. 282 was given in [1920](/wiki/1920_in_association_football \"1920 in association football\") to a club named Football Club Racing Club Lokeren (nicknamed Racing FC), but the team stopped its activity the next year. On [22 January 1923](/wiki/1923_in_association_football \"1923 in association football\") Racing Club Lokeren was founded. Between [1945](/wiki/1945_in_association_football \"1945 in association football\") and [1951](/wiki/1951_in_association_football \"1951 in association football\"), it had a slight name change (to Racing Athletiek- en Football Club Lokeren) and the new name since 1951 was Koninklijke Racing Club Lokeren. Due to financial problems, the fusion with the other team from the town (Koninklijke Standaard FC Lokeren) became necessary in [1970](/wiki/1970_in_association_football \"1970 in association football\"). The new club was then named Koninklijke Sporting Club Lokeren.\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png/250px-KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png)](/wiki/File:KSC_Lokeren_Performance_Chart.png)\\n\\nHistorical chart of KSC\\xa0Lokeren league performance\\n\\nIn 2000, the club merged with Koninklijke Sint-Niklaas SKE to form Sporting Lokeren Sint-Niklaas Waasland. The latest name change occurred in [2003](/wiki/2003_in_association_football \"2003 in association football\"), with the province name added to the club name.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*]\\n\\nIn 2018, Sporting Lokeren were relegated to the [First Division B](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_B \"Belgian First Division B\"), the second tier of Belgian football.[[4]](#cite_note-4) In 2019, the club was taken over by a group led by Louis de Vries and Alexander Janssen, taking the positions of president and CEO respectively.\\n\\nOn 20 April 2020, the club was declared bankrupt during the 2019–20 season.[[2]](#cite_note-hln-2) Lokeren had outstanding debts of €5 million and was not able to pay its staff and players anymore.\\n\\nOn 22 April 2020, Lokeren agreed to merge with KSV Temse to form a new club in [K.S.C. Lokeren-Temse](/wiki/K.S.C._Lokeren-Temse \"K.S.C. Lokeren-Temse\") and to start in the [Second Amateur Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Amateur_Division \"Belgian Second Amateur Division\"), the national fourth Westerlo season\")* | |\\n\\n**[Koninklijke](/wiki/Koninklijk \"Koninklijk\") Voetbal Club Westerlo** (Dutch pronunciation: [[ˈkoːnɪŋkləkə ˈvudbɑl ˌklʏp ˈʋɛstərloː]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Dutch \"Help:IPA/Dutch\"); often simply called **Westerlo**) is a [Belgian](/wiki/Belgium \"Belgium\") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football \"Association football\") club located in the municipality of [Westerlo](/wiki/Westerlo \"Westerlo\") in the province of [Antwerp](/wiki/Antwerp_(province) \"Antwerp (province)\"). Since [1997–98](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_1997-98 \"Belgian First Division 1997-98\"), Westerlo has been mostly playing in the [Belgian Pro League](/wiki/Belgian_Pro_League \"Belgian Pro League\"), save for a short stint in the [Belgian Second Division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Division \"Belgian Second Division\") between 2012 and 2014. Their highest finish is a 6th place in [1999–00](/wiki/Belgian_First_Division_1999-2000 \"Belgian First Division 1999-2000\"), [2003–04](/wiki/2003%E2%80%9304_Belgian_First_Division \"2003–04 Belgian First Division\") and [2008–09](/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_Belgian_First_Division \"2008–09 Belgian First Division\"). They have won one [Belgian Cup](/wiki/Belgian_Cup \"Belgian Cup\"). The only player who has ever been called up for the [Belgium national football team](/wiki/Belgium_national_football_team \"Belgium national football team\") while at Westerlo is [Toni Brogno](/wiki/Toni_Brogno \"Toni Brogno\") (7 caps, all of them while at Westerlo).\\n\\nThe club was founded in 1933, receiving the [matricule number](/wiki/Football_in_Belgium#Matricule_numbers \"Football in Belgium\") 2024. Their colours are yellow and blue. They play their home matches at the [Het Kuipje](/wiki/Het_Kuipje \"Het Kuipje\").\\n\\nHistory\\n-------\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=K.V.C._Westerlo&action=edit&section=1 \"Edit section: History\")]\\n\\n**K.V.C. Westerlo** was founded in the city of Westerlo by students in 1917, and it was named Sportkring De Bist Westerlo. After five years of existence, the club retired. The club **Bist Sport** was created in 1931 and it changed its name to Sportkring Westerlo two years later. At that time. some players left the club to found **Westerlo Sport**, the ancestor of **K.V.C. Westerlo**. In 1939, the club won its [league](/wiki/Belgian_Provincial_leagues \"Belgian Provincial leagues\") for the first time. Five years later, Sportkring Westerlo and dissident Westerlo Sport decided to merge in spite of the rivalry between the teams, and the new club was called **V.C. Westerlo**.\\n\\nIt became champion of the [Antwerp second division](/wiki/Belgian_Provincial_leagues \"Belgian Provincial leagues\") in 1960. Eight years later it played its first season at the national level in [Promotion](/wiki/Belgian_Promotion \"Belgian Promotion\") and it won its league to play the [third division](/wiki/Belgian_Third_Division \"Belgian Third Division\") in 1969. At the end of the season, Westerlo missed a third title in a row, finishing second behind [Eupen](/wiki/K.A.S._Eupen \"K.A.S. Eupen\"). The next year, the club was relegated after the playoff and it stayed in the Promotion for ten seasons. The club then underwent two relegations in a row and thus played in the Antwerp second division in 1982–83. Westerlo was then promoted for three consecutive years to qualify for the third division once again. In 1993, the club promoted to the [second division](/wiki/Belgian_Second_Division \"Belgian Second Division\") and then to the first division in 1997. In 1996, the club added the prefix *[Koninklijke](/wiki/Koninklijk \"Koninklijk\")* (meaning \"Royal\" in [Dutch](/wiki/Dutch_language \"Dutch language\")) to its name.\\n\\nOn 18 June 2019 it was officially announced that the club was taken over by Turkish businessman Oktay Ercan. He immediately made it clear that KVC Westerlo will remain a regional family club, and that more attention will be paid to the social dimension and sporting ambitions. Ercan expressed his commitment in 2019 to a year-long plan called \\'KVC Westerlo 2024\\'.[[2]](#cite_note-2)\\n\\nStadium\\n-------\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=K.V.C._Westerlo&action=edit&section=2 \"Edit section: Stadium\")]\\n\\nWesterlo plays its home matches at [Het Kuipje](/wiki/Het_Kuipje \"Het Kuipje\"), which is Dutch for \"The Cockpit\". \"Serbian Cyrillic alphabet\"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian \"Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian\")) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegro \"Montenegro\") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football \"Association football\") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](/wiki/Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor \"Radanovići, Kotor\"), municipality of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor \"Kotor\"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League \"Montenegrin Second League\").\\n\\nHistory\\n-------\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=1 \"Edit section: History\")]\\n\\nThe first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League \"Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)\") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia \"FR Yugoslavia\") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia \"1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia\"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  \\nAfter [Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 \"Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006\"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League \"Montenegrin First League\"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta \"FK Zeta\") and [Budućnost Podgorica](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica \"FK Budućnost Podgorica\"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn\\'t achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  \\nOFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom \"FK Kom\") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar \"FK Mornar\") in [Bar](/wiki/Bar,_Montenegro \"Bar, Montenegro\") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  \\nIn the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Montenegrin_Cup \"2016–17 Montenegrin Cup\"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 \"FK Sutjeska Nikšić\") 1–0.  \\nAfter 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League \"2019-20 Montenegrin First League\"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League \"Montenegrin Second League\").\\n\\n### First League Record\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=2 \"Edit section: First League Record\")]\\n\\nSee also: [Participants of Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League#All_time_tables \"Montenegrin First League\")\\n\\nFor the first time, OFK Grbalj played in Montenegrin First League on season [2006–07](/wiki/2006%E2%80%9307_Montenegrin_First_League \"2006–07 Montenegrin First League\").
